The '''1672 Ayuman Cup''', recognised retrospectively as the 4th edition of the '''[[FLLA World Cup]]''', was an international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the leading Ayuman football associations. It was held in [[Emara]], across [[Ayuma]], from 4 June to 2 July 1672, and was won by the hosts, [[Emara]], who defeated [[Lycroa]] 6–3 in the [[#Final|final]] at the Rivostan Grand Stadium to claim their first title.<ref name="heritage-overview">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1672/overview|title=The 1672 Ayuman Cup: tournament overview|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 March 1763}}</ref>

The tournament was staged under the older title of the Ayuman Cup, the name the competition bore before the [[FLLA]] was constituted and the contest was relaunched and renamed the [[FLLA World Cup]] at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]]; the seven continental confederations did not yet exist, and all ten entrants were drawn from [[Ayuma]]. It was the fourth edition to be completed, the [[1664 FLLA World Cup|1664 tournament]] having been awarded but abandoned before play on the outbreak of the [[Great Imperial War]].<ref name="heritage-rename">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/history/early-competition-names|title=From the Ayuman Cup to the FLLA World Cup: the early names of the competition|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=12 February 1764}}</ref>

The 1672 edition was contested for the original rotating '''[[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]]''', which had been held by every champion since the inaugural edition of 1656 and which was presented to the victorious Emaran side at the close of the final. No bespoke permanent trophy was awarded; the permanent-trophy tradition that came to characterise the competition began only with the Solana at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]], after the loss of the original cup in [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]] in 1688.<ref name="heritage-trophy">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/trophies/the-andah-cup|title=The original Andah Cup and the early Ayuman Cup editions|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=2 July 1764}}</ref>

==Host selection==

The 1672 tournament was awarded to [[Emara]] by a congress of the Ayuman national associations, the informal body that organised the competition before the foundation of the [[FLLA]]. Emara had entered each of the previous editions without reaching the latter stages, and the award of hosting rights was seen as recognition of the growing strength of the Emaran game. The Emaran organisers undertook to stage the finals across five cities, with the principal matches held in the capital, [[Rivostan]].<ref name="heritage-host">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1672/host|title=1672 Ayuman Cup: the award of hosting rights to Emara|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 March 1763}}</ref>

==Format==

The 10 entered teams were divided into two groups of five for the group stage. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing the other four sides in its group; two points were awarded for a win and one for a draw, in line with the scoring system then in use. The top two teams in each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]], while the remaining three were eliminated. Where teams finished level on points, places were determined first by goal difference and then by goals scored.

The knockout stage took the form of two semi-finals, in which each group winner was drawn against the runner-up of the other group, followed by a [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] and the [[#Final|final]]. Knockout ties were single-elimination matches played over 90 minutes; a tie level at the end of normal time was extended by a single 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]], with any tie still level after extra time to be settled by a replay rather than by a [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], a procedure not yet in use. No replay proved necessary in 1672.

The continental confederations that later structured the [[FLLA World Cup]] had not yet been established, and qualification was settled under the informal arrangements of the period; as host nation, [[Emara]] took part automatically. ==Venues==

Five stadiums in five host cities, all in [[Emara]], were used in the final tournament. The principal venue was the Rivostan Grand Stadium in the capital, [[Rivostan]], which staged the opening match and the final and was the largest ground in use. The two semi-finals were divided between the Khalzhun Arena in [[Khalzhun]] and the Shaikuv Stadium in [[Shaikuv]], with the [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] held at Yilovka Park in [[Yilovka]]. The remaining group-stage fixtures were shared between these grounds and the smallest venue, at [[Borzhai]].<ref name="heritage-venues">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1672/venues|title=Host stadiums of the 1672 Ayuman Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=21 March 1763}}</ref>

==Squads==

Each participating association registered a squad of eighteen players, two of whom were required to be goalkeepers; the smaller squads of the period reflected the limited substitution rules then in force, under which a single replacement was permitted only for an injured goalkeeper. A total of 180 players were registered for the tournament.<ref name="heritage-squads">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1672/squads|title=1672 Ayuman Cup: registered squads|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=21 March 1763}}</ref>

==Match officials==

The organising congress appointed a panel of referees and linesmen drawn from the associations not represented in the latter stages of the competition. The opening match was refereed by Aldous Verin of [[Verusa]], and the final by Mikol Renz of [[Eldjo]], the senior official of the tournament. The small officiating pool of the period meant that several referees took charge of fixtures involving teams from neighbouring associations, though never from their own.<ref name="heritage-officials">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1672/officials|title=Match officials of the 1672 Ayuman Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=21 March 1763}}</ref>

==Group stage==

The two groups were each contested as a single round-robin. The top two teams in each group advanced to the knockout stage; points were awarded on the two-points-for-a-win system in use at the time, with goal difference and then goals scored used to separate teams level on points.

All dates are given in the local time of the host cities.

==Knockout stage==

The knockout stage involved the four teams that advanced from the group stage. Each group winner was drawn against the runner-up of the other group: [[Emara]], the winners of Group B, met the Group A runner-up [[Estijan]], while the Group A winners [[Praesyu]] met the Group B runner-up [[Lycroa]]. The two losing semi-finalists contested a [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] on the day before the final.

===Final===

The final was held at the Rivostan Grand Stadium on 2 July 1672 before an estimated crowd of 20,000. [[Emara]] took the lead early through Dragomir Volzhen, the tournament's leading scorer, and led 3–1 by the hour through Ivor Kazhan and Milorad Tschev, with [[Lycroa]] replying through Tomas Calmar. Volzhen completed his hat-trick and Tschev added a second, and although Calmar struck again and Andrej Veldt pulled one back, Emara ran out 6–3 winners. The victory secured Emara's first title, won on home soil, and the original [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]] was presented to the Emaran captain at the close of the match.<ref name="heritage-final">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1672/final|title=The 1672 Ayuman Cup final: Emara 6–3 Lycroa|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 March 1763}}</ref>

==Statistics==

===Goalscorers===

A total of 100 goals were scored in 24 matches, an average of 4.17 per match. The leading scorer was the Emaran forward Dragomir Volzhen, who scored ten goals across the tournament, including three in the final. No formal individual awards were presented at the 1672 edition: the leading-player, top-scorer and best-goalkeeper prizes (the [[FLLA World Cup#Awards|Vairan Ball, Marskval and Bastion]]) were not instituted until the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]], and the figures below are recognised retrospectively in the [[FLLA]]'s heritage records.<ref name="heritage-stats">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1672/statistics|title=1672 Ayuman Cup statistical record|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=21 March 1763}}</ref>

==Trophy and significance==

The 1672 edition was the fourth completed staging of the competition and the second to be won by its host. The cup that Emara lifted was the original rotating [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]], the same trophy that had been contested since the inaugural edition of 1656; under the custom of the period the champion held it until the next tournament, when it passed to the new winners.<ref name="heritage-trophy" />

Emara's victory on home soil was the high point of Emaran football of the early Ayuman Cup era, and the runners-up [[Lycroa]] reached the final of the competition for the first time. The original cup was contested for a further three editions before it was lost in [[Alzurian Union|Alzuria]] in 1688; when the competition was relaunched and renamed the [[FLLA World Cup]] at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]], the host association instead commissioned a bespoke permanent trophy, beginning the permanent-trophy tradition that has characterised the competition ever since.<ref name="heritage-rename" />
